mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher than baseline during low FEDFUNDS periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate increased demand in the housing market, suggesting broader economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not follow a 5% YoY increase in HOUST (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment rates signal a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Low UNRATE does not correlate with positive 20-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production suggests supply constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO below 100 does not lead to negative returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment and low unemployment indicate a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Joint rise in PAYEMS and UNRATE does not predict positive returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Increased real consumer spending suggests strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: RSAFS above 680000 does not lead to positive returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates in a tightening cycle may slow economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: High FEDFUNDS does not predict negative returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High inflation combined with high federal funds rates may indicate tightening that slows growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS both high does not predict negative returns (Rank IC < 0.03).
